hook.line: The building site next door starts at six every morning. Tomás has had enough, and Spanish has vivid ways to say so without swearing.
hook.es: Estoy hasta la coronilla del ruido.
hook.en: I'm sick to death of the noise.

examples.es: Estoy hasta la coronilla de sus excusas.
examples.en: I'm sick to death of his excuses.

examples.es: Estoy hasta la coronilla de que me llamen a las diez de la noche.
examples.en: I'm sick to death of them calling me at ten at night.

examples.es: Me saca de quicio que llegue siempre tarde.
examples.en: It drives me up the wall that he's always late.

examples.es: Me puso de mal genio que no me avisaran.
examples.en: It put me in a foul mood that they didn't tell me.

examples.es: Estoy hasta la coronilla de esperar.
examples.en: I'm sick to death of waiting.

examples.es: Hoy Vale está de mal genio.
examples.en: Vale is in a bad mood today.

rule:
Three friendly ways to say you've had enough.
*Estar hasta la coronilla de* + noun or infinitive: "sick to death of". The top of your head is full. For what someone does, add *que* + subjunctive: *de que me llamen*.
*Sacar de quicio*: the thing is the subject, you are *me*. *Me saca de quicio que llegue tarde.*
*Estar de mal genio*: in a bad mood.
Spain's *hasta las narices* is understood here, but you will hear *coronilla* more.
smallPrint: Teachers call these idiomatic expressions of annoyance. They take *que* + subjunctive when they react to something someone does.

readAndPick.es: Estoy hasta la coronilla de sus excusas.
options: I'm sick to death of his excuses.
His excuses made me happy.
I'm making excuses up to the top.

readAndPick.es: Me saca de quicio que llegue siempre tarde.
options: I'm always late and it bothers him.
He took me out of the house when he was late.
It drives me up the wall that he's always late.

readAndPick.es: Estoy hasta la coronilla de esperar.
options: I'm happy to wait.
I'm sick to death of waiting.
I'm still waiting.

readAndPick.es: Hoy Vale está de mal genio.
options: Vale is feeling brilliant today.
Vale has a bad temper by nature.
Vale is in a bad mood today.
Vale has a bad temper by nature.
Vale is in a bad mood today.
Vale is a great cook.

readAndPick.es: Me puso de mal genio que no me avisaran.
options: It put me in a good mood that they told me.
It put me in a bad mood that they didn't tell me.
I told them about my bad mood.

readAndPick.es: Estoy hasta la coronilla de que me llamen a las diez de la noche.
options: I'm sick to death of calling them at ten at night.
I'm sick of the ten o'clock night call.
I'm sick to death of them calling me at ten at night.

readAndPick.es: El ruido de la obra me saca de quicio.
options: The noise from the building site drives me up the wall.
I make the noise at the building site.
The building site is far from the noise.

yourTurn.prompt: Choose *de* or *con*, then type the whole sentence: Estoy hasta la coronilla ___ sus excusas. (I'm sick to death of his excuses.)
yourTurn.answer: Estoy hasta la coronilla de sus excusas.
yourTurn.why: The thing you're sick of follows *de*.

yourTurn.prompt: Choose *llamen* or *llaman*, then type the whole sentence: Estoy hasta la coronilla de que me ___ a las diez de la noche. (I'm sick to death of them calling me at ten at night.)
yourTurn.answer: Estoy hasta la coronilla de que me llamen a las diez de la noche.
yourTurn.why: A feeling about what others do takes *que* and the subjunctive.

yourTurn.prompt: Type it in Spanish: I'm sick to death of waiting.
yourTurn.answer: Estoy hasta la coronilla de esperar.
yourTurn.why: When it's you doing the verb, *de* plus the infinitive is enough.

yourTurn.prompt: Type it in Spanish: It drives me up the wall that he's always late.
yourTurn.answer: Me saca de quicio que llegue siempre tarde.
accept: Me saca de quicio que siempre llegue tarde.
yourTurn.why: The lateness is the subject of *saca*, and you are *me*.

yourTurn.prompt: Type it in Spanish: Vale is in a bad mood today.
yourTurn.answer: Hoy Vale está de mal genio.
accept: Vale está de mal genio hoy.
yourTurn.why: A mood for today takes *está de*.

yourTurn.prompt: Say it to a friend: *Me saca de quicio que llegue siempre tarde.* becomes: It drives you up the wall that he's always late.
yourTurn.answer: Te saca de quicio que llegue siempre tarde.
accept: Te saca de quicio que siempre llegue tarde.
yourTurn.why: Swap *me* for *te*: the person who is annoyed is *you*.

yourTurn.prompt: Say it about Vale: *Estoy hasta la coronilla de sus excusas.* becomes: Vale is sick to death of his excuses.
yourTurn.answer: Vale está hasta la coronilla de sus excusas.

pitfalls.wrong: Estoy hasta la cabeza de sus excusas.
pitfalls.right: Estoy hasta la coronilla de sus excusas.
pitfalls.why: Almost. The idiom is fixed: *coronilla* is the very top of the head.

pitfalls.wrong: Estoy hasta la coronilla que me llamen.
pitfalls.right: Estoy hasta la coronilla de que me llamen.

pitfalls.wrong: Yo saco de quicio que llegue tarde.
pitfalls.right: Me saca de quicio que llegue tarde.
pitfalls.why: Almost. The lateness does the driving, so it is the subject, and you are *me*.

personal: Tell me what drives you up the wall. Use *Me saca de quicio que...* or *Estoy hasta la coronilla de...*
